title: Per-camera + per-class night suppress (e.g. parked vehicles from OUTSIDE_BACK_SOLAR)
context: Operator 2026-09-22 19:42 EDT alert 6645c41d-3551-4181-b066-4ffbc2c7d6be: motion at night from OUTSIDE_BACK_SOLAR triggered a vehicle alert, frames too dark/grainy to confirm, vehicle_features.confidence=0.0. Existing MOTION_GATE_NIGHT_SUPPRESS_ENABLED=1 and FARMSURV_QUIET_HOURS_ENABLED=0 are GLOBAL — they affect all cameras. We need a per-camera, per-class allowlist of cameras (and optionally classes) that get dropped at the motion-gate layer during night hours, so a parked-vehicle camera doesn't spam Telegram at 3am while a person at the front door still alerts.
shipping_definition: Two new env knobs read at runtime by infra/quick_classifier.py (motion-gate layer) and infra/quiet_hours.py (TG-dispatch layer, defense-in-depth):
FARMSURV_NIGHT_SUPPRESS_CAMERAS — comma-separated camera slugs (e.g. OUTSIDE_BACK_SOLAR). Empty default = current behavior. (1=ON/OFF not applicable; presence-or-absence gates the rule.)
FARMSURV_NIGHT_SUPPRESS_CLASSES — optional comma-separated class names (e.g. vehicle). Empty default = match any class.

Motion-gate drop rule: when is_night_at_edt(timestamp) AND camera_id in NIGHT_SUPPRESS_CAMERAS AND (class in NIGHT_SUPPRESS_CLASSES OR NIGHT_SUPPRESS_CLASSES is empty) -> drop the alert at infra/quick_classifier.py BEFORE YOLO gate, with a structured log line {level: INFO, event: 'night_suppressed', camera_id, class, reason: 'camera+class match'}.

TG-dispatch defense: same check in infra/quiet_hours.py so an alert that slipped past the gate (e.g., race with config reload) still gets silenced at TG send time. Log event {level: INFO, event: 'tg_night_suppressed', ...}.
Both layers log the suppression but do NOT write a per-alert event.json (US-068a's record) — only alerts that survive to the end get an event.json. Suppressed alerts are noise, not audit history.
Existing 178 unit + 17 e2e tests continue to pass.
No change to PID 25850 listener until operator restarts (deferred per AGENTS.md Step 4 directive: do not disrupt in-flight kanban work; restart before declaring live).
Per AGENTS.md env-var-naming rule: presence-or-absence for the camera list, no boolean. Add to .env.example with example values showing 'empty = disabled' inline.
design_principles: Layered suppression. The motion-gate is the primary stop; TG-dispatch is the belt-and-suspenders. Either alone is sufficient, both is safer.
Additive only. Default values (empty lists) reproduce current behavior exactly. No surprise changes for cameras not in the list.

Camera+class OR-only. If both lists are configured, BOTH must match (camera in list AND class in list OR no class list). Class-only without camera list is rejected at config-load time with a loud warning ('config says suppress class vehicle globally — is that what you meant?').
Read-only mirror: US-068b3 (gate resource via MCP) surfaces current suppress lists. No write tool yet; operator edits via env file.
No per-event audit. A suppressed alert is by definition noise — no event.json written. The audit log is for events that reached a decision point.

Twilight buffer still applies. is_night_at_edt() already accounts for FARMSURV_NIGHT_TWILIGHT_BUFFER_MIN=0 (current). If operator wants BACK_SOLAR suppressed earlier in the evening, they bump that knob globally — out of scope here.

stories.title: Quick classifier: per-camera + per-class night suppress
scope: New env vars (add to .env.example with comment lines showing empty = disabled):
# FARMSURV_NIGHT_SUPPRESS_CAMERAS: comma-separated camera slugs to suppress at night. Empty = current behavior (no per-camera suppression). Example: OUTSIDE_BACK_SOLAR
# FARMSURV_NIGHT_SUPPRESS_CLASSES: optional comma-separated class names to suppress at night. Empty = suppress all classes on listed cameras. Example: vehicle
Helper function _parse_csv_env(name: str) -> list[str] in infra/env_utils.py: read os.environ.get(name, ''), strip whitespace, split on comma, drop empties. Returns [] if unset or empty.

Helper function _night_suppress_match(camera_id: str, class_name: str) -> bool in infra/quick_classifier.py: reads the two env vars via _parse_csv_env, returns True if camera_id in cameras AND (classes empty OR class_name in classes).

In classify_frame() or its caller: when is_night_at_edt(timestamp) AND _night_suppress_match(camera_id, class_name) -> return a 'suppressed' sentinel before YOLO gate. Log INFO {event: 'night_suppressed', camera_id, class_name, reason: 'camera+class match'}.

If FARMSURV_NIGHT_SUPPRESS_CAMERAS is empty but FARMSURV_NIGHT_SUPPRESS_CLASSES is non-empty: log WARNING {event: 'night_suppress_class_without_camera', classes: ...} at boot and continue with no-op behavior. Don't silently drop class-only.

stories.title: TG-dispatch: defense-in-depth night suppress
scope: Reuse _parse_csv_env and _night_suppress_match from US-069a (import from infra/quick_classifier).

In in_quiet_hours(camera_id, dt, class_name=None): if class_name is provided AND _night_suppress_match(camera_id, class_name) -> return True (treat as quiet hours). Log INFO {event: 'tg_night_suppressed', camera_id, class_name}.
If class_name is None (legacy caller), fall back to current global is_night_at_edt logic — do not silently suppress without class info.

stories.title: .env.example + AGENTS.md update
scope: .env.example: add the two new knobs with comment lines per AGENTS.md env-var-naming convention (presence-or-absence or CSV examples, not 1=ON/0=OFF).
AGENTS.md: append to 'Runtime (snapshot)' section listing new env knobs + the OUTSIDE_BACK_SOLAR use case as the canonical example.
Cross-reference V2-068b3 (MCP gate resource) — when that ships, the suppress lists become visible via get_gate_config().

estimated_complexity: small — three stories, each under ~50 LOC. Two read-only env knobs, two-layer suppression, no behavioral change to cameras not in the list. Reviewer + QA cycle on each story.
